name: Platform Adoption Essentials
description: The Platform Adoption Essentials baseline establishes the universal foundation for platform transformations, extending the Project Essentials baseline with platform-specific concerns across the three Areas of Concern.

focuses.name: Value
focuses.description: Focuses on business justification, financial management, and organizational alignment.

focuses.name: Solution
focuses.description: Encapsulates the design, provisioning, optimization, and the hosted items running on the platform foundation.

focuses.name: Endeavor
focuses.description: Governs the execution of the transformation, encompassing people, processes, and policies.

alphas.name: Platform Value And Economics
alphas.description: The financial and outcome-based justification and accounting for the platform.

states.name: Modeled
states.description: Financial needs and potential values are recognized.

states.name: Allocated
states.description: Costs and benefits are logically modeled.

states.name: Sustained
states.description: The economic model is approved.

alphas.name: Requirements
alphas.description: The capabilities, features, and constraints the platform must satisfy.

states.name: Conceived
states.description: The need for a specific asset is identified.

states.name: Bounded
states.description: The scope of the requirements is defined.

states.name: Coherent
states.description: Requirements are clear, consistent, and logical.

states.name: Acceptable
states.description: Stakeholders agree the requirements meet their needs.

states.name: Addressed
states.description: The platform satisfies the established requirements.

states.name: Fulfilled
states.description: All requirements are successfully delivered and operational.

alphas.name: Platform
alphas.description: The unified system of infrastructure, compute resources, networking, storage, and foundational services that provide the technical foundation for hosting and operating platform assets. This includes clusters, virtual machines, container orchestrators, databases, message queues, load balancers, and other infrastructure components that form the substrate upon which applications and services run.

states.name: Architecture Selected
states.description: The foundational structural boundaries, hosting paradigms, and technical strategies are formally selected and agreed upon by enterprise architecture.

states.name: Baselined
states.description: Core capabilities, shared services, and network perimeters are logically mapped, with constraints and integration points clearly defined.

states.name: Provisioned
states.description: The foundational infrastructure and shared environments have been instantiated and are ready to support integration, though not yet accepting live production workloads.

states.name: Ready
states.description: The platform is fully operational, resilient, and successfully integrated with consumption interfaces, enabling autonomous developer self-service.

states.name: Hosting Assets
states.description: The platform is actively, securely, and reliably supporting external application workloads serving live enterprise traffic.

states.name: Evolving
states.description: The platform architecture autonomously adapts using predictive scaling and continuous feedback, while obsolete legacy capabilities are gracefully decoupled and decommissioned.

states.name: Retiring
states.description: The platform is being systematically decommissioned, with workloads migrated to alternative platforms and infrastructure safely removed.

alphas.name: Platform Consumption Interface
alphas.description: The means by which consumers discover, access, and consume platform capabilities, including developer portals, service catalogs, CLI tools, APIs, SDKs, documentation hubs, golden path templates, and self-service workflows that abstract the underlying platform complexity and provide a developer-friendly consumption experience.

states.name: Envisioned
states.description: The desired interface is conceptualized.

states.name: Scoped
states.description: Interface capabilities are defined.

states.name: Available
states.description: The interface is accessible.

states.name: Self Service
states.description: Consumers can independently use the interface.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: The interface dynamically adapts based on deep user telemetry, providing a frictionless, self-service experience that actively minimizes developer cognitive load.

alphas.name: Platform Asset
alphas.description: The individual applications, services, databases, message streams, or workloads that consumers create, deploy, and operate on the platform infrastructure. These are the business-value-delivering artifacts that run atop the platform substrate and are accessed through the platform consumption interface.

states.name: Identified
states.description: The need for a specific asset is identified.

states.name: Specified
states.description: The asset's architectural footprint, resource dependencies, and required platform integrations are explicitly detailed and approved.

states.name: Provisioned
states.description: The asset is created or acquired.

states.name: Integrated
states.description: The asset is successfully configured to natively consume platform-provided shared services (e.g., logging, identity, routing) within non-production environments.

states.name: Operational
states.description: The asset is in active use.

states.name: Value Yielding
states.description: The asset is demonstrably delivering measurable value to platform consumers and the broader enterprise.

states.name: Retiring
states.description: The asset is being systematically decommissioned and replaced, with dependencies migrated and resources reclaimed.

states.name: Scoped
states.description: The need for governance is recognized.

states.name: Documented
states.description: Initial policies are defined.

states.name: Audited
states.description: Policies are actively applied.

alphas.name: Platform Risk And Compliance
alphas.description: Measures the business risk evaluation, security posture validation, and compliance mitigation maturity.

states.name: Identified
states.description: Basic security risks and compliance needs are listed.

states.name: Assessed
states.description: Detailed risk assessment matrices and compliance mappings are documented.

states.name: Mitigated
states.description: Scenario-based behavioral guides mitigate specific user risks.

states.name: Automated
states.description: Automated compliance auditing and security posture checks are in place.

activitySpaces.name: Monitor Value Realization
activitySpaces.description: Track KPIs such as deployment frequency, MTTR, and developer adoption rates to proactively manage bottlenecks and prove continuous ROI.

activitySpaces.name: Manage Platform Economics
activitySpaces.description: Define chargeback/showback models, right-size infrastructure, optimize costs through FinOps practices, and transition from CapEx to OpEx.

activitySpaces.name: Establish Secure Guardrails
activitySpaces.description: Shift security left, embed Zero Trust principles, and codify compliance requirements into automated scanning tools to ensure secure-by-default platform operations.

activitySpaces.name: Define Platform Capabilities
activitySpaces.description: Distill stakeholder feedback into actionable requirements and define the Thinnest Viable Platform (TVP) to avoid over-engineering.

activitySpaces.name: Architect and Build the Foundation
activitySpaces.description: Establish declarative provisioning (IaC), build CI/CD pipelines, configure connectivity, deploy orchestration engines, and instantiate the six pillars of platform engineering.

activitySpaces.name: Operate and Evolve the System
activitySpaces.description: Execute Day-2 operations using SRE practices, manage observability telemetry, ensure high availability, and continuously evolve the platform.

activitySpaces.name: Develop the Golden Paths
activitySpaces.description: Build Internal Developer Portals (IDPs), intuitive CLIs, and automated scaffolding templates to drastically reduce cognitive load and enable autonomous self-service.

activitySpaces.name: Integrate Toolchain Services
activitySpaces.description: Specify, acquire, and securely integrate individual platform assets ensuring seamless interoperability with established Golden Paths.

activitySpaces.name: Implement Policy-as-Code
activitySpaces.description: Translate manual governance rules into automated, machine-readable policies that execute within deployment pipelines without impeding velocity.

activitySpaces.name: Decommission and Retire
activitySpaces.description: Safely decouple, deprecate, and remove obsolete platform assets, legacy infrastructure, or older operational processes to minimize technical debt and resource waste.

competencies.name: Engineering
competencies.description: The ability to design, build, and implement technical solutions.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands fundamental software architecture and basic cloud infrastructure concepts.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can implement basic infrastructure components, deployment scripts, or single-node services based on established guidance.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can independently design distributed components, author declarative configuration templates, and build automated pipelines for platform ecosystems.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can architect complex, multi-tenant platform foundations, resolve systemic integration challenges, and abstract underlying infrastructure complexities for consumers.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops entirely new engineering paradigms or open-source technical solutions for hyperscale platform orchestration.

competencies.name: Platform Security And Compliance Enforcement
competencies.description: The ability to design, implement, and automate security policies, access controls, and compliance checks within the platform.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands basic security principles and compliance requirements.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can configure basic security settings and access controls based on documented procedures.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can independently design and implement comprehensive security architectures and automate compliance auditing.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can adapt security strategies to address novel threats and complex, multi-cloud environments.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops new paradigms for platform security and proactive threat hunting.

competencies.name: Platform Strategic Alignment
competencies.description: The ability to align platform capabilities and roadmap with broader business goals, economic models, and enterprise architecture.

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the high-level business drivers for the platform.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can articulate how specific platform features support identified business opportunities.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can develop and manage platform roadmaps that demonstrably drive business value and ROI.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can pivot platform strategy in response to shifting market conditions or major organizational changes.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Pioneers new platform business models or economic strategies that redefine enterprise value.

competencies.name: Site Reliability
competencies.description: The ability to apply software engineering principles to operations, ensuring platform reliability, scalability, and performance (SRE).

levels.name: Basic
levels.description: Understands the concepts of SLIs, SLOs, and basic incident response.

levels.name: Applies
levels.description: Can participate in incident response and implement basic monitoring alerts.

levels.name: Masters
levels.description: Can independently design robust monitoring systems, define effective SLOs, and lead complex incident resolutions.

levels.name: Adapts
levels.description: Can architect highly resilient, self-healing systems and establish enterprise-wide SRE practices.

levels.name: Innovating
levels.description: Develops novel approaches to chaos engineering or predictive reliability modeling.

narrativeTypes.name: The Three-Act Structure & StoryBrand
narrativeTypes.description: Positions the consumer as the Hero and the Platform Engineering team as the Guide utilizing the defined approach.

narrativeElements.name: Act I: The Hero and the Problem
narrativeElements.description: Identifying the consumer and their pain points.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Identify the primary consumer (the Hero) and detail the specific friction or problem they face.

narrativeElements.name: Act II: The Guide and the Plan
narrativeElements.description: The platform team offers a solution.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Introduce the Platform Engineering team as the Guide who provides a clear, paved-path approach or plan.

narrativeElements.name: Act III: Call to Action and Success
narrativeElements.description: Execution and outcome.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Describe the call to action for the consumer to adopt the plan, and the successful outcome of doing so.

narrativeTypes.name: User story
narrativeTypes.description: A brief, informal explanation of a software feature written from the perspective of the end user.

narrativeElements.name: As a [role]
narrativeElements.description: This identifies the specific persona or role interacting with the feature. It avoids the generic term **the user** to provide context on their technical ability, permissions, and needs.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to define constraints. Instead of saying "user," say "First-time Visitor" or "System Administrator." This helps the developers understand if the UI should be "idiot-proof" or "power-user focused."

narrativeElements.name: I want to [perform some action]
narrativeElements.description: This is the intent or the feature itself. It describes the action the user wants to take within the software.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Keep this focused on the **what,** not the **how.** Avoid mentioning specific UI elements like **click a red button.** Focus on the functional capability you are giving them.

narrativeElements.name: So that [I can achieve some goal]
narrativeElements.description: This is the purpose. It explains the underlying problem the user is trying to solve or the value they hope to gain.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to justify the work. If you can’t find a compelling **So that** statement, the feature might not be worth building. It also helps developers suggest better technical solutions if they understand the ultimate goal.

narrativeTypes.name: Epic
narrativeTypes.description: A well-structured Epic provides a "north star" for the team, ensuring everyone knows why a large project exists and what success looks like.

narrativeElements.name: Summary
narrativeElements.description: A clear, punchy title and a one-sentence elevator pitch that describes the high-level initiative.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Treat this as the project's identity. Use it in stakeholder meetings and roadmap views to provide an instant understanding of what is being built without getting bogged down in details.

narrativeElements.name: Strategic Intent
narrativeElements.description: This section explains how this Epic aligns with the company's broader business goals or quarterly objectives (OKRs).
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to justify the budget and resource allocation. If you can't link the Epic back to a specific business value (e.g., "Increasing retention by 10%"), it shouldn't be an Epic.

narrativeElements.name: User Personas
narrativeElements.description: A list of the primary and secondary users who will be impacted by this large-scale change.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to keep the scope focused. When brainstorming features, ask: "Does this specific feature serve the personas listed in the Epic?" If not, it belongs in a different Epic.

narrativeElements.name: High-Level Requirements
narrativeElements.description: These are not detailed stories yet, but rather the broad capabilities the system must have once the Epic is finished.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use these as "themes" to help you brainstorm the individual User Stories later. They serve as the framework for your backlog.

narrativeElements.name: Success Metrics
narrativeElements.description: The quantitative data points that will prove the Epic was a success after it is released.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Use this to define the "Definition of Done" for the entire project. Instead of saying "when the code is finished," use "when the checkout conversion rate hits 5%."

narrativeTypes.name: Essay Narrative
narrativeTypes.description: A cohesive narrative format that guides the reader carefully through the evidence for and against a proposition before reaching a conclusion.

narrativeElements.name: Introduction
narrativeElements.description: The start of the essay used to contextualise the work and grab the attention of the reader.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Explain how the topic sits within the framework of the subject area as a whole. Outline the structure of your essay very briefly, but do not give your conclusions away on the first page.

narrativeElements.name: Defining Key Concepts
narrativeElements.description: A section establishing the interpretation of central concepts without relying on dictionary definitions.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Relate in your own words how the terms you will be using are to be interpreted within the context of your essay.

narrativeElements.name: Presenting Evidence
narrativeElements.description: The core discussion where secondary works are evaluated and viewpoints are balanced against each other.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Be selective in your choice of evidence and use signposting language to guide your reader. Quote sparingly, paraphrase occasionally, and summarise often to integrate other people's ideas into your own argument.

narrativeElements.name: Conclusion
narrativeElements.description: The closing section that synthesises the presented evidence and forms a direct response to the assignment title.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Draw the threads of your argument together. Do not bring in new evidence in your concluding paragraphs or try to cram in ideas that you have not developed fully.

narrativeTypes.name: Report Narrative
narrativeTypes.description: A formal, informative structure broken down into sections and sub-sections to order and communicate relevant information in an easily navigable way.

narrativeElements.name: Executive Summary
narrativeElements.description: A stand-alone summary of the entire report's purpose, methodology, findings, conclusions, and recommendations.
narrativeElements.howToUse: This should be the last thing that you write. Keep it concise (usually a paragraph or two and always less than a page) to enable the reader to make an informed decision about whether they want to read the report itself.

narrativeElements.name: Introduction
narrativeElements.description: Explains the rationale for undertaking the work reported on, the background, and the scope of the report.
narrativeElements.howToUse: State what the report is about, define how it meets the requirements of the brief, and explain your research methods.

narrativeElements.name: Methods
narrativeElements.description: A clear description of how the investigation was carried out and why specific methods were chosen.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Write this section concisely but thoroughly. Provide step-by-step details in such a way that a reader could replicate the research you have done.

narrativeElements.name: Results and Findings
narrativeElements.description: A purely factual presentation of the research data using text, graphs, tables, or diagrams.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Present the findings of your research as simply as possible. Save your interpretation of the results for the Discussion section.

narrativeElements.name: Discussion
narrativeElements.description: The section that brings everything together by showing how the findings relate to the purpose of the report and previous research.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Interpret the results, showing how they respond to the brief explained in the introduction. Mention if there were any problems or unexpected results and how they were solved.

narrativeElements.name: Recommendations
narrativeElements.description: Suggestions for a future course of action based on the evidence and conclusions.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Make recommendations that solve problems or help to develop a new strategy. Make an effort to sound authoritative and certain in your choices.

narrativeTypes.name: SDLC
narrativeTypes.description: Software Development Lifecycle pattern for systematic technical delivery from requirements through maintenance.

narrativeElements.name: Plan
narrativeElements.description: Requirements gathering and project planning phase.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Define objectives, scope, requirements, and success criteria for the initiative.

narrativeElements.name: Design
narrativeElements.description: Architecture and detailed design phase.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Establish technical architecture, design patterns, and implementation approach.

narrativeElements.name: Build
narrativeElements.description: Implementation and construction phase.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Develop, configure, and assemble the solution components.

narrativeElements.name: Test
narrativeElements.description: Validation and quality assurance phase.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Verify functionality, performance, security, and integration through testing.

narrativeElements.name: Deploy
narrativeElements.description: Release and deployment phase.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Roll out to production environment with appropriate deployment strategy.

narrativeElements.name: Maintain
narrativeElements.description: Operations and continuous improvement phase.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Monitor, optimize, patch, and evolve the solution in production.

narrativeTypes.name: Build-Measure-Learn
narrativeTypes.description: Lean Startup cycle for validating assumptions through rapid experimentation and feedback.

narrativeElements.name: Build
narrativeElements.description: Create minimum viable solution.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Develop smallest increment that can test key hypothesis or assumption.

narrativeElements.name: Measure
narrativeElements.description: Collect data and feedback.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Instrument, observe, and gather quantitative and qualitative evidence.

narrativeElements.name: Learn
narrativeElements.description: Analyze and decide next iteration.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Synthesize findings, validate or invalidate hypothesis, pivot or persevere.

narrativeTypes.name: Design-Build-Run-Optimize
narrativeTypes.description: Architectural lifecycle for infrastructure and platform engineering spanning conception through continuous improvement.

narrativeElements.name: Design
narrativeElements.description: Architecture definition and planning.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Define architecture, topology, technology choices, and capacity planning.

narrativeElements.name: Build
narrativeElements.description: Provisioning and configuration.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Deploy infrastructure, configure systems, establish integrations and connectivity.

narrativeElements.name: Run
narrativeElements.description: Operations and steady-state management.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Monitor health, respond to incidents, maintain availability and performance.

narrativeElements.name: Optimize
narrativeElements.description: Continuous improvement and evolution.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Tune performance, reduce costs, enhance capabilities based on operational insights.

narrativeTypes.name: Crawl-Walk-Run
narrativeTypes.description: Maturity progression model for incremental capability building and adoption.

narrativeElements.name: Crawl
narrativeElements.description: Initial capability establishment.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Establish foundational capability with limited scope, manual processes, learning focus.

narrativeElements.name: Walk
narrativeElements.description: Capability refinement and scaling.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Expand scope, introduce automation, standardize processes, build confidence.

narrativeElements.name: Run
narrativeElements.description: Mature, optimized operation.
narrativeElements.howToUse: Full automation, enterprise scale, optimization focus, continuous evolution.
